exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. caesarean section)
Gestational age at birth (preterm vs. term)
Type of infant feeding (exclusive breastfeeding vs. exclusive formula feeding at 6 weeks)
outcome: Risk of developing paediatric-onset inflammatory bowel disease (PIBD)
cohort: All children born in Scotland between 1981 and 2017 (n=2,013,851)
finding: In this nationwide Scottish cohort study, no association was found between mode of delivery, gestational age at birth, or exclusive formula feeding at 6 weeks and the development of PIBD.
mod_finding: Children delivered vaginally did not have an altered risk of developing PIBD compared with those delivered by caesarean section (adjusted HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.84-1.08).
